title: Pointed etale scheme neighbourhoods of an algebraic-space geometric point are cofiltered
statement: Work in the universes and small-site convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ with $\Omega$ an algebraically closed field. Let $\mathcal N_{\bar x}$ have objects $(U,\bar u)$, where $U\to X$ is an etale map from a scheme in the small etale site of $X$ and $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ lifts $\bar x$; an arrow $(V,\bar v)\to(U,\bar u)$ is a map $h:V\to U$ over $X$ satisfying $h\bar v=\bar u$. This category is small in the containing universe and cofiltered: it is nonempty, any two objects receive arrows from a common object, and any two parallel arrows $h_1,h_2:(V,\bar v)\rightrightarrows(U,\bar u)$ are equalized by an arrow $(W,\bar w)\to(V,\bar v)$. Thus its opposite is filtered in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Tag 04JW (lemma-cofinal-etale), including the final assertion restricting to scheme neighbourhoods; paragraph after Tag 04JY (definition-stalk).

proof.text: Use the small skeleton of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ fixed in [def-weil-size-convention]. Its objects and arrows form sets in the containing universe. For each object $U$, its lifts of $\bar x$ form a subset of the set $\operatorname{Hom}_S(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,U)$. The objects of $\mathcal N_{\bar x}$ therefore form a set-indexed union of sets, and its arrows are subsets of the site hom sets. Thus $\mathcal N_{\bar x}$ is small in that universe. In the following constructions a scheme neighbourhood may be replaced by its chosen site representative: if $a:U_0\xrightarrow{\sim}U$ is the representative isomorphism, replace $\bar u$ by $a^{-1}\bar u$ and each incident arrow by its composite with $a$ or $a^{-1}$. All pointed commutativity and equalizing equations are preserved.

source.place: Tag 04JW (lemma-cofinal-etale), restriction to objects of the small site; paragraph after Tag 04JY (definition-stalk), with the project universe convention.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $A\to X$ with $A$ a scheme, using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Its base change $E=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\times_X A\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is a surjective etale morphism of schemes by the scheme-test meaning in that definition, so $E$ is nonempty. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] to this scheme morphism and the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$; its fibre is $E$ itself. Thus $E$ has a component $\operatorname{Spec}L$ for a finite separable extension $L/\Omega$. This extension equals $\Omega$: for each $a\in L$, a nonzero annihilating polynomial over $\Omega$ factors into linear factors by repeated application of the root property in [def-weil-algebraic-closure]; its value at $a$ is zero in a field, so one factor is zero and $a$ lies in $\Omega$. The component inclusion therefore gives a section $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to E$. Composing with $E\to A$ gives $\bar a$ with image $\bar x$, hence an object $(A,\bar a)$ of the neighbourhood category (after Step 1).

source.place: Tag 04JW (lemma-cofinal-etale), final proof paragraph applied to an atlas of X; morphisms.tex Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field), part (2).

proof.text: Given $(U_1,\bar u_1)$ and $(U_2,\bar u_2)$, form $P=U_1\times_X U_2$ as a sheaf fibre product. It is represented by a scheme by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. Its projection $P\to U_1$ is representable etale by base change of $U_2\to X$, and $P\to X$ is representable etale by composition, using the same cited statement. The pair $(\bar u_1,\bar u_2)$ defines a map $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to P$ because both components have composite $\bar x$. Its two projections are exactly the prescribed lifts. Consequently $(P,(\bar u_1,\bar u_2))$ is a scheme neighbourhood with pointed arrows to both given objects. Apply Step 1 if a site representative is required.

source.place: Tag 04JW (lemma-cofinal-etale), proof of (1); base change and composition from Tags 03FU and 03FT, in the representable scheme-test form.

proof.text: Given $h_1,h_2:(V,\bar v)\rightrightarrows(U,\bar u)$, set $P=U\times_X U$, a scheme etale over $X$ by the construction of Step 3. The map $r=(h_1,h_2):V\to P$ is a scheme map over $X$. Since $V\to X$ and $P\to X$ are representable etale, the final clause of [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests] says that $r$ is etale. Let $\Delta:U\to P$ be the diagonal and form the scheme fibre product $W=V\times_{r,P,\Delta}U$ using [def-pc-fibre-product]. Its projection $q:W\to U$ is etale by base change of $r$; hence $W\to U\to X$ is representable etale, by the base-change, scheme-comparison and composition clauses of [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. The equality $r\bar v=(\bar u,\bar u)=\Delta\bar u$ gives the lift $\bar w=(\bar v,\bar u)$ to $W$. If $p:W\to V$ is the other projection, the fibre-product equation $(h_1p,h_2p)=(q,q)$ proves $h_1p=h_2p$, and $p\bar w=\bar v$. Thus $p:(W,\bar w)\to(V,\bar v)$ is the required pointed equalizer arrow. No separatedness of $U\to X$ or closedness of its diagonal is used. Replace $W$ by its representative as in Step 1.

source.place: Tag 04JW (lemma-cofinal-etale), proof of (2), its displayed fibre-product square; etale permanence is Tag 03FV.

proof.text: Step 2 gives nonemptiness, Step 3 gives common incoming arrows for every pair of objects, and Step 4 gives an incoming equalizing arrow for every pair of parallel arrows. These are precisely the cofilteredness axioms. Reversing arrows gives nonemptiness, common outgoing arrows and outgoing equalizing arrows in $\mathcal N_{\bar x}^{\mathrm{op}}$, which are the filteredness axioms in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The smallness assertion is Step 1.
